newsitem.title: INDIA: India NSE shares close up on end-account covering.
newsitem.headline: India NSE shares close up on end-account covering.

text.p: Indian shares listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Bombay ended higher on Tuesday as speculators covered short positions on the last day of the account, traders said.
NSE's 50-stocks index climbed 11.18 points to a provisional close of 972.89. The Bombay and Calcutta stock exchanges were closed for a Jain festival.
Traders said punters covered short positions in NSE pivotals including ITC, BSES and IPCL, driving prices higher at close.
Select bids by foreign funds in stocks including motorcycle and scooter makers TVS Suzuki and Bajaj Auto also cheered sentiment, traders said.
"Funds were buyers in select stocks at lower levels but speculators jumped on the bandwagon as prices started rising," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
They said funds were buyers in blue chips like HPCL, Cadbury, MTNL, Hindustan Lever and IPCL.
Traders said there were sellers in lubricants maker Castrol, hospitality firm Hotel Leelaventure and cement giant Associated Cement Companies.

The share price of ACC has fallen more than 5.0 percent in two trading sessions. Analysts say a series of cost increases including fuel, freight and power have led to escalating production costs at a time when signs of oversupply in the cement sector are evident in several regions.
Last week, the 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) slumped 160.70 points or 4.8 percent to 3347.37 after the government failed to deliver anticipated tax reliefs.
Traders expect the market to open weak on Wednesday.
